LESSON: WRITING 11.5.1 SPELLING ANTONYMS, SYNONYMS, AND NUMBERS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.5: Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to tell the synonyms and antonyms of words? 2. Why is it important to write numbers in words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.5.1 Spelling antonyms, synonyms, and numbers together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital literacy is developed as the learner searches for more antonyms and synonyms from the internet to boost their ability

to use digital devices.

 Collaboration is enhanced as the learner generates a list of antonyms and synonyms in collaboration with peers.

Values:
Unity is cultivated as the learner collaborates with peers to search for more examples of antonyms and synonyms.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Effective communication is improved as the learner uses antonyms, synonyms, and figures in words correctly in writing.

Link to other subjects

The learner relates the concepts of antoyms, synonyms and writing of numbers to other learning areas such as Kiswahili,

Mathematics and Integrated Science.
